# Benchmarks

## Per-example gradients

Median wall-clock time to get the gradient of every example in a batch: one
backward pass per example (`loop`), `vmap` over `grad`, and forward hooks
with a single backward pass. Single precision.
Measured on Apple M5 Max with torch 2.14.1.

| model | device | batch | loop (ms) | vmap (ms) | hooks (ms) | vmap speed-up | hooks speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | cpu | 64 | 4.72 | 0.52 | 0.26 | 9x | 18x |
| gpt 2x64 | cpu | 64 | 58.90 | 8.12 | 7.00 | 7x | 8x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | cpu | 256 | 18.98 | 0.91 | 0.38 | 21x | 49x |
| gpt 2x64 | cpu | 256 | 229.82 | 19.88 | 18.81 | 12x | 12x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | mps | 64 | 18.59 | 1.20 | 1.14 | 15x | 16x |
| gpt 2x64 | mps | 64 | 158.07 | 7.97 | 3.60 | 20x | 44x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | mps | 256 | 67.96 | 1.09 | 1.01 | 62x | 68x |
| gpt 2x64 | mps | 256 | 434.42 | 20.86 | 4.56 | 21x | 95x |

## Single precision against double

Relative error of each quantity computed in float32, against the same
quantity in float64 on the CPU: the norm of the difference over the norm
of the reference. For the solves, the iteration counts are those of
conjugate gradient to a relative residual of 1e-6 in float32 and 1e-10 in
float64, and the residual is the true one of the float32 solution.

### mlp 196-32-32-10, 7,690 parameters

## Preconditioning conjugate gradient

Iterations of conjugate gradient to a relative residual of 1e-8 against the
damped Gauss-Newton matrix, for three right-hand sides at once. The
preconditioners are the damped inverses of K-FAC, of EK-FAC, and of the true
matrix with the interactions between layers removed. Double precision, models
at their random initialisation. A star marks a solve that did not converge.
